subject: Medicine
summary: Renal stones are crystalline deposits in the kidney that can cause sudden, severe pain and urinary symptoms. Diagnosis relies on imaging and urine analysis, while management balances pain control, hydration, and addressing underlying metabolic causes.

sections.p: Renal stones are mineral aggregates that form within the renal collecting system. Diagnosis is confirmed by non‑contrast CT, ultrasound, or plain X‑ray, and urine microscopy shows crystals.

faq.q: Can a kidney stone be asymptomatic?
faq.a: Yes, many stones are small and pass without pain, or are discovered incidentally on imaging.

faq.q: What dietary changes help prevent stones?
faq.a: Increase fluid intake, limit sodium and animal protein, moderate oxalate foods, and avoid excessive vitamin C.
